how_to_tell_apart: The bundle has no ready lang_words_id.json, so contrasts were taken from the Indonesian FrequencyWords list and standard Malay–Indonesian lexical differences. Prefer Malay-leaning items: boleh (Indonesian often bisa), awak or anda (versus kamu), mahu or nak (versus mau), pukul for clock time (versus jam), kereta for a car (in Indonesian kereta is usually a train and a car is mobil), telefon, wang, emel, and titles encik, puan and tuan. Saya, tidak, yang and terima kasih are shared and should not swing the decision. Colloquial tak is common in Malaysia but also turns up in informal Indonesian, so it is only a weak hint.
